rationale: This program is the Shootout matrix-multiply kernel: a tiny, function-sparse program dominated by tight arithmetic inner loops over dense arrays, so runtime overhead in hot loops is the binding constraint while code size and control-flow complexity are minimal. SUB is cheap per-op and raises diversity of the arithmetic-heavy inner loops, so it gets high SecurityGain/DiversityGain with low size/correctness sensitivity; SPLIT is nearly free and fragments the simple loop bodies for cheap resistance, so its RuntimeCost/SizeCost sensitivities are kept very low to let it trigger broadly. BCF and FLA are the most expensive control-flow transforms and would multiply the cost of the hottest loops, so their RuntimeCost and (for BCF) SizeCost weights are high, meaning they only apply where cost features are weak; FLA is retained at moderate strength because flattening the loop nests still meaningfully disrupts static analysis of the kernel. IBR offers good disassembly/analysis resistance but inserts dispatch overhead in hot loops, so it is enabled with a moderately high RuntimeCost weight; ICALL is low-risk and diversifies indirect-call sites even though this program has few calls. IGV targets global data, which this global-free scalar kernel barely uses, so it is included with uniformly low weights and will effectively be disabled by feature scoring rather than omitted.
